context: Final deep machine/project audit, authority reconciliation, artifact consolidation, failure-prevention and maintenance-roadmap classification.
finalObjective: Establish one canonical project-control root with reconstructable origin→current history, evidence-backed current capabilities, classified machine artifacts, authoritative release identity, explicit non-blocking boundaries, and durable controls against authority drift.

downloads.limitation: Downloads/My Project broad content search timed out in some attempts; targeted project-name searches are high-confidence negative evidence but not every-byte proof.
downloads.unrelatedGenericDirectMethodHits: Scientific RETURN_R013A files; deliberately not moved.

remoteCommanderSafetyBackups.rationale: Duplicating the safety store into the project root would add hundreds of MB without increasing project truth.

historicalWorktrees.cleanupAttempt: git worktree remove attempted and failed with Windows Permission denied

artifactClassification.canonicalDeliveryPolicy: Tagged public-version product artifacts only + README + exact current public checksum asset.
preservedIntermediate: v1.3.1 intermediate Windows C453... and Linux A50F... -> archive/superseded-artifacts/v1.3.1-intermediate

findings.claim: Canonical delivery checksum serialization was stale/misaligned with v1.4.0 exact public checksum asset.
findings.rootCause: Ignored/local delivery state survived across release worktrees; root text checksum content and exact public CRLF asset serialization were conflated.
findings.prevention: Pin exact public checksum asset source/hash in consolidation and verify RELEASE checksums.artifact raw SHA.

findings.claim: windows/RELEASE.json publication state could remain stale because release_metadata_audit used a brittle contiguous status substring.
findings.rootCause: The old guard tested literal PUBLISHED_VERIFIED while current status is PASS_FINAL_PUBLISHED_INSTALLED_VERIFIED_V1_4_0.
findings.prevention: Explicit publication metadata in root/platform release records; structural published+verified detection; publication-field comparison; checksum-artifact raw-hash verification.

findings.claim: Three Brain-recorded final-evidence raw SHA-256 values are worktree-byte-serialization specific, not stable tracked-text identities.
evidence: git diff main audit/v1.4.0-finalize = no content diff
findings.prevention: Use Git blob/commit identity for tracked text; use raw worktree SHA only when serialization/EOL is explicitly pinned.

findings.claim: Linux updater checksum verification is sound but has weaker defense-in-depth than Windows because it does not cross-check GitHub API asset digest.
findings.proposal: Future release: require exact-one Linux asset and SHA256SUMS asset, API digest == SHA256SUMS == downloaded ZIP SHA-256.

findings.claim: Router Gateway L2TP/IPsec health fallback uses TCP/443 as a generic endpoint reachability heuristic, not a protocol-aware L2TP/IPsec probe.
findings.proposal: Relabel as generic endpoint reachability or add bounded UDP 500/4500 diagnostics; do not imply authenticated tunnel success.

github.limitation: Full branch-protection administration endpoint returned 403 to the GitHub integration; branch object exposed protected status and required checks.

validationBoundaries: Physical-router authenticated tunnel success remains model/firmware dependent.
HTTP/3 application-level QUIC remains unproven on the validation host; UDP/443 QUIC configuration/runtime is verified.
DoH3/DoQ/DoT are software-supported but were not promoted because current-network isolated resolution failed.

roadmap.current: v1.4.0 maintenance authority; audit/control metadata reconciliation

exactNextAction: Commit/push audit and control-metadata reconciliation, pass protected PR checks, merge to main; do not mutate immutable v1.4.0 tag/assets. Runtime improvements belong to a future release branch.
